notes: Oil broke lower through a Gulf stalemate, the Shenzhen trilateral produced an energy-flows declaration that does not name Iran, and the Strait logged a fourth hull hit in four days. Oil: Wed 18 Nov Brent Jan-27 settled 91.95 (-1.19, -1.28%), WTI Dec-26 83.26 (-2.75, -3.2%), lowest close since 26 Aug, after EIA crude +3.38 mb (vs an expected small draw), gasoline +5.19 mb; Brent-WTI spread widened $1.80 to 8.93 (DTN ties it to tanker freight constraining US export arb); Brent down ~a fifth in November; Rigzone/Bloomberg: 'very limited appetite to buy the dip', market 'acclimated' to Gulf flare-ups; Dec WTI expires Fri 20 Nov (next run's front is Jan-27). Thu 19 Nov Asia Brent 92.12 (+0.18%) at 02:37 GMT. Shenzhen (19 Nov): Trump told Xi and Putin 'We're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon' (09:25Z); Trump said he and Xi strongly support oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz (06:20Z; 'oil should move through the Strait of Hormuz' at 13:58 local); the trilateral 'Peace Declaration' (released 18:55 Shenzhen) commits to increasing production and supply of oil/refined products and 'stable energy flows', UN reform, court immunities and 'a nuclear war cannot be won' - no Iran, Hormuz or Middle East paragraph. Trump to Fox from Shenzhen (aired ~02:00Z 19 Nov): the Islamabad MOU was 'a waste of time', 'I want a deal that can be lasting', 'I'm going to finish it off - soon. One way or the other', 'We talked to them... they want to make a deal', blockade 'the most effective thing we've done', 'real indication' Iran is 'looking at gas... bio', 'if it does happen, we wipe them out', and 'we'll see what happens after January 1st' - no timetable, no mechanism, no mediator named. Israel: CENTCOM's Cooper met Zamir and Mossad's Gofman in Tel Aviv 18 Nov ('deepening strategic and operational cooperation'); Mako (via Gulf News 19 Nov) says Trump is still considering a joint attack with Israel on Iran, no decision, to be discussed after the Asia trip; senior US official 'all options are available'. Maritime: UKMTO 212-26 - a tanker struck in the engine room by an unknown projectile 6 nm N of Khasab at 16:45Z 18 Nov, outbound, all crew safe (alert 02:30 UAE 19 Nov, time-late); UKMTO 211 (posted 18 Nov, time-late) covers the 17 Nov evening ADNOC L&S hit 13 nm N of Khasab - the vessel is now identified by Vanguard Tech as NAVIG8 MESSI (Liberia, product tanker, ADNOC L&S commercial manager), with India's Sonowal saying the entire crew is 'safe and accounted for, with no serious injuries' vs ADNOC's 1 missing / 11 injured - unresolved; TARA GAS 'still burning and drifting southeast' (NAVAREA IX 451-26, 15:00Z 18 Nov), one Indian seafarer still missing. Iran's regular navy (20:21Z 18 Nov) claims three 'violating' tankers hit mines east of Hormuz and caught fire; IRGC navy (13:52 Tehran 19 Nov) claims two 'violating supertankers' carrying >4 mb hit mines and exploded; none matched by UKMTO, no sinking or death confirmed. CENTCOM (18 Nov) extends the blockade to ship-to-ship transfers of Iran-origin cargo ('stopped, boarded, diverted, captured'; 'use of force'); NAVCENT: neutral transit to non-Iranian destinations not impeded. hormuz.now 18 Nov 21:49Z: 41 crossings/7d = 5.9/day (7% of 84.8), 17 Nov full day 5, 18 Nov 6 so far, tankers 12/7d (1.7/day, 4%), 371 tankers/43 VLCC visible; straits.live 20:30Z: 43 AIS-visible vessels holding. Gulf front: Iran attacks on Kuwait (Ali Al-Salem) and Bahrain 18 Nov intercepted, US Embassy Bahrain alert (four attempts in a week), State reissues Saudi/Bahrain warnings; Saudi-led coalition hits 60 Houthi targets, intercepts cruise missiles toward Riyadh 18 Nov and a Houthi missile's debris damages the 80-storey PIF tower in Riyadh 19 Nov; Reuters: Saudi preparing for the Yemen war into 2027; Yemen designates the Houthis a terrorist organisation; Belgium to seek EU listing. Plumbing: Baghaei rebukes Grossi on 'double standard'; DNI Clayton: Iranian threats 'dramatically increased'; Khanna/Ansari to oppose funding without a bar on offensive Iran operations (11 Dec deadline); OFAC 18 Nov Counter Terrorism (Hezbollah gold/charity network) under 'Operation Economic Outcast Targets Iran's Proxy Networks'. No Qatar/Oman/Pakistan/Witkoff item dated in gate beyond Trump's 'we talked to them'. Net: Strait closed, no deal, a confirmed US-Iran strike exchange answered on both sides by interceptions rather than escalation, a fourth tanker hit with crew safe, the trilateral silent on Iran, and oil at a 12-week low.

Brent-WTI spread widened $1.80 to 8.93 (DTN: elevated tanker freight constraining US export arb).

items.name: UKMTO-confirmed incidents in gate: 1 new - Warning 212-26, tanker struck in the engine room by an unknown projectile ~6 nm N of Khasab at 16:45Z 18 Nov, outbound, all crew safe (alert issued 02:30 UAE 19 Nov, time-late); plus UKMTO 211 published 18 Nov (time-late) for the 17 Nov evening ADNOC L&S hit, now identified as NAVIG8 MESSI - already counted 11-18
items.source: Gulf News 19 Nov (Khasab tanker article, UKMTO 212-26 footnote); Treadstone 71 19 Nov (211/212 summary); gCaptain 18 Nov 11:12 PST (UKMTO warning 211 PDF, NAVAREA IX 451-26); Riviera 18 Nov (211 time-late, Sonowal); Khaleej Times live 18 Nov 16:29 UAE ('3 Indian sailors safe after attack on another oil tanker')
items.note: (1) NEW - UKMTO 212-26: unnamed tanker, outbound, struck in the engine room ~6 nm north of Khasab at 1645Z 18 Nov; 'All crew members were reported safe and accounted for'; extent of damage unknown; no attribution; alert delayed by local-authority reporting. Fourth hull hit near Khasab in four days (TARA GAS 16 and 17 Nov, NAVIG8 MESSI 17 Nov, this one 18 Nov). (2) UKMTO 211 (posted 18 Nov, time-late): tanker struck by an unknown projectile ~13 nm N of Khasab on 17 Nov, fire later extinguished, SAR for a missing crew member - this is the ADNOC L&S vessel recorded 11-18 (count unchanged); Vanguard Tech identifies it as NAVIG8 MESSI (Liberia-flag product tanker, ADNOC L&S commercial manager; previously hit by UAV with TARIF on 13 Aug). Crew status conflict: India's Sonowal on X - 'the entire crew, are safe and accounted for, with no serious injuries reported' (Khaleej 16:29 UAE: three Indian sailors safe) vs ADNOC's 1 unaccounted / 11 injured; Riviera had no ADNOC confirmation at publication - unresolved. (3) TARA GAS: NAVAREA IX 451-26 at 15:00Z 18 Nov 'still burning and drifting southeast' ~5.7 nm off Khawr Ghub Ali; 24 rescued, 2 hospitalised, one Indian seafarer still missing; no death confirmed. So the 11-18 'two missing' may be one (Tara Gas) if Sonowal is right on Navig8 Messi. Neither UKMTO entry describes a mine strike; UKMTO logged no sinking.

items.note: Counted as one Iran-proxy action: the listings carry SDGT tags only (no IRAN/IFSR program tag) and target a Lebanon/Turkey gold and charity network funding Hezbollah; Treasury frames it as part of the Iran 'Operation Economic Outcast' series. No Iran-tagged (shadow fleet, petrochemical, IRGC) designation dated 18-19 Nov. Scorer may treat as 0 for Iran-direct sanctions pressure. No 19 Nov OFAC action surfaced by run time.

items.name: Shenzhen trilateral (19 Nov): Trump tells Xi and Putin 'We're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon' (09:25Z); Trump and Xi 'strongly support' oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz (06:20Z); three-way 'Peace Declaration' (18:55 local) pledges to increase oil/refined-product production and supply and 'stable energy flows', UN reform, court immunities, 'a nuclear war cannot be won' - no Iran, Hormuz or Middle East paragraph
items.headline: Live - Iran will not get nuclear weapon, Trump says at summit with Xi and Putin / APEC live: Trump, Xi, Putin commit to 'stable energy flows', nuclear talks / 'Nuclear war cannot be won': Full text of China, Russia and US 'Peace Declaration'
items.claim: Iran International (19 Nov 09:25Z): Trump told Putin and Xi the US would not let Iran get a nuclear weapon - 'We're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon'; (06:20Z) Trump said he and Xi strongly support oil flowing through the Strait of Hormuz, Xi said he remained committed to keeping China-US relations on the 'correct course'. leprivatebanker (11:35 GMT): Trump at 13:58 local said he and Xi felt strongly that 'oil should move through the Strait of Hormuz'; the joint statement released at 18:55 in Shenzhen says China, the US and Russia 'will increase the production and supply of oil' with 'no volumes, quotas or start dates' and does not mention OPEC+ or Iran. The National (11:21Z) summarises the four-point declaration: (1) UNSC permanent members commit to UN reform; (2) increase production and supply of refined petroleum products 'for the benefit of all nations' and reaffirm 'the importance of stable energy flows'; (3) state consent and immunities, ICC must not abuse jurisdiction; (4) 'a nuclear war cannot be won and must never be fought', a three-way dialogue on nuclear risk reduction and non-proliferation. Al Jazeera: Chinese state media call it a 'peace declaration'. Fox (18 Nov 9:40pm ET): Trump reportedly will not press Beijing or Moscow to stop sharing targeting intelligence with Iran. Iran International summary (18 Nov): Trump said the US does not need help from China or Russia to end the war with Iran.
items.source: Iran International liveblog 19 Nov 06:20Z and 09:25Z; leprivatebanker 19 Nov 11:35 GMT; The National 19 Nov 11:21Z; Al Jazeera APEC liveblog 19 Nov (header, updated 11:55); Fox live 18 Nov 10:14pm EST; DTN 18 Nov (market pre-read)
items.note: The summit the market had priced as a de-escalation venue (DTN: risk premium 'compressed ahead of' it) produced an energy-supply pledge without numbers and a non-proliferation line, with Iran named only in Trump's own remarks; no Chinese or Russian statement on Iran or Hormuz surfaced, no joint Iran language, no mediation role assigned. Scorer: a 'stable energy flows' pledge by Iran's two largest patrons alongside the US is a soft T1 signal; absence of Iran in the text is the harder fact. Full declaration text not reproduced (The National summary used); time.com and newsdrum analyses unreachable. Oil post-declaration print not yet surfaced.

items.name: Trump to Fox from Shenzhen (aired ~02:00Z 19 Nov): the Islamabad MOU was 'a waste of time' ('they can't be trusted'), 'I want a deal that can be lasting', 'I'm going to finish it off - soon. One way or the other', 'We talked to them... they want to make a deal', blockade 'the most effective thing we've done', 'real indication' Iran is 'looking at gas... bio' - 'if it does happen, we wipe them out', 'we'll see what happens after January 1st'
items.headline: Trump calls Islamabad MOU 'waste of time,' vows to end Iran war soon / Iran War Updates: Trump says Tehran may be working on chemical or biological weapons
items.claim: Iran International (19 Nov 01:42Z) and Fox live (18 Nov ~9:14-9:40pm ET): in a Fox News interview given Wednesday from Shenzhen, Trump called the preliminary US-Iran agreement (the Islamabad memorandum) 'a waste of time' that 'delayed things a little bit' - 'We got to know them very well during that period, and we got to know that they can't be trusted'; 'I want a deal that can be lasting'; 'I'm going to finish it off - soon. One way or the other, we'll finish it off'; the naval blockade is 'the most effective thing we've done'; 'What we're doing is the right thing'; on Vance being pulled from Iran talks: 'He's doing a very good job. No.' Gulf News (19 Nov 08:21 UAE): Trump said 'We talked to them' and Tehran 'want[s] to make a deal', giving no terms, timetable or mechanism. On WMD: 'There is a real indication that Iran is looking at gas, is looking at bio'; asked if DC should be alarmed - 'I don't think so. No, I mean, look, if it does happen, we wipe them out', 'I give you my word. Absolutely'; and 'We're going to have a new year coming up and we'll see what happens after January 1st' (Fox/Times of Israel). Iran International (18 Nov): the Intelligence Ministry said it awaits a chance to avenge Khamenei's killing; parliament's national security spokesman: 'Today, the enemy does not know on which continent the Islamic Republic's missiles will land.' No Iranian response to the interview surfaced by run time.
items.source: Iran International 19 Nov 01:42Z; Fox live 18 Nov 10:14pm EST; Gulf News live 19 Nov 08:21 UAE; Times of Israel liveblog 19 Nov; CBS live 18 Nov (headline)
items.note: First Trump statement in gate that both (a) asserts a live channel ('we talked to them') and (b) disowns the only signed framework (Islamabad MOU) while flagging a January 1 horizon - consistent with the 15 Nov 'status quo' posture but with a harder 'finish it off' edge; no mediator (Qatar/Oman/Pakistan), no Witkoff, no venue or date named. Pairs with the Mako joint-attack report (see Israel hit). Scorer decides whether 'lasting deal' + 'after January 1' reads as a deadline or as drift.

items.name: US-Israel coordination: CENTCOM's Adm. Cooper meets IDF chief Zamir in Tel Aviv, then a trilateral with Mossad's Gofman - 'deepening strategic and operational cooperation' (18 Nov); Mako (via Gulf News 19 Nov 12:33 UAE): Trump still considering a joint attack with Israel on Iran, no decision, to be discussed after the Asia trip; senior US official: 'all options are available to President Trump to ensure that Iran never has a nuclear weapon'; DNI Clayton: Iranian threats 'have dramatically increased'
items.headline: Middle East war: Riyadh skyscraper damaged, tanker hit near Oman as Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes / CBS live 18 Nov 1:08 PM ET
items.claim: CBS (18 Nov 1:08pm ET): CENTCOM commander Adm. Brad Cooper met Israeli Chief of Staff Lt. Gen. Eyal Zamir in Tel Aviv, followed by a trilateral with Mossad Director Roman Gofman; the Israeli statement refers to 'deepening strategic and operational cooperation between the two militaries'. Gulf News (19 Nov 12:33 UAE): Israeli site Mako, citing two unnamed sources, reported Trump is still considering a joint attack with Israel on Iran; a senior US official said 'all options are available to President Trump to ensure that Iran never has a nuclear weapon'; Mako says no decision has been made and the issue will be discussed after the Asia trip; Netanyahu has urged the US to push strikes on Iran; Gofman met US officials in Washington the previous week. CBS (12:02pm ET): DNI Jay Clayton told the House Homeland Security Committee Iranian threats 'have dramatically increased'. CBS (~1:40pm ET): US Embassy Bahrain security alert citing at least four attempted Iranian strikes in the past week; Gulf News: State Department reissued Saudi and Bahrain warnings calling for 'heightened vigilance'. Gulf News (10:57 UAE 19 Nov): Democrats Khanna and Ansari will oppose any funding package that does not 'explicitly prohibit funds from being used for offensive operations in Iran' (11 Dec deadline). Times of Israel's 'PM reportedly calls Iran op unavoidable' headline surfaced but the retrieved page did not contain that entry.
items.source: CBS live 18 Nov 12:02, 1:08, ~1:40 PM ET; Gulf News live 19 Nov 10:57 and 12:33 UAE; Khaleej Times live 18 Nov 21:55 UAE; Times of Israel liveblog 19 Nov (headline only)
items.note: Strike-planning plumbing rather than a strike: the Cooper-Zamir-Gofman meeting is the first in-gate dated US-Israel operational contact since the 'US and Israel draw up plans' item (Day 260, already recorded), and the Mako report is single-sourced Israeli media with an explicit 'no decision'. The 'after the Asia trip' and Trump's 'after January 1st' lines bound the window. Clayton's threat testimony and the embassy alerts are the homeland side of the same posture. No Hegseth/CENTCOM statement on a wider strike surfaced.

items.name: Fourth tanker hit near Khasab in four days: UKMTO 212-26 - unnamed outbound tanker struck in the engine room by an unknown projectile ~6 nm N of Khasab at 16:45Z 18 Nov, all crew safe (alert 02:30 UAE 19 Nov); UKMTO 211 published for the 17 Nov ADNOC hit, vessel identified as NAVIG8 MESSI (Liberia, product tanker) - India's Sonowal says entire crew 'safe and accounted for, with no serious injuries' vs ADNOC's 1 missing / 11 injured; TARA GAS 'still burning and drifting southeast' (NAVAREA IX 15:00Z), one Indian seafarer still missing
items.headline: Tanker Struck by Unknown Projectile Near Oman in Latest Strait of Hormuz Incident / TARA GAS Burning Off Oman as Another Tanker Attack Leaves 11 Injured / Update: all crew 'are safe and accounted for' following strike on tanker in Strait of Hormuz
items.claim: Gulf News (19 Nov): UKMTO reported a tanker 'struck by an unknown projectile in its engine room' approximately 6 nautical miles north of Khasab, Oman, at 1645 UTC on 18 November while sailing outbound; 'All crew members were reported safe and accounted for'; extent of damage and environmental impact unknown; UKMTO issued the alert at 2:30am Thursday after a delayed report from local authorities and advised vessels to 'exercise caution and report suspicious activity'; warning number 212-26. gCaptain (18 Nov 11:12 PST): NAVAREA IX warning 451-26 at 1500 UTC says TARA GAS is 'still burning and drifting southeast' about 5.7 nm off Khawr Ghub Ali; ADNOC L&S did not name its vessel but Vanguard Tech identified it as the Liberian-flagged product tanker NAVIG8 MESSI, which ADNOC L&S commercially manages (hit with TARIF by UAV on 13 Aug); UKMTO warning 211 places that strike ~13 nm north of Khasab on 17 Nov, fire later extinguished. Riviera (18 Nov): UKMTO attack report 211 is 'time-late' and mentions SAR for a missing crew member; India's Sonowal on X said for Navig8 Messi 'the entire crew, are safe and accounted for, with no serious injuries reported'; Riviera had not received ADNOC's confirmation. Khaleej (16:29 UAE 18 Nov): three Indian sailors safe after attack on another oil tanker. Treadstone 71: neither UKMTO entry describes a mine strike; no sinking logged.
items.source: Gulf News 19 Nov; gCaptain 18 Nov 11:12 PST; Riviera 18 Nov; Treadstone 71 19 Nov; Khaleej Times live 18 Nov 10:46, 12:58, 16:29 UAE; straits.live 18 Nov brief
items.note: Maritime tempo: TARA GAS (16, 17 Nov), NAVIG8 MESSI (17 Nov), unnamed tanker (18 Nov) - all on the Omani side of the outbound lane north of Khasab, all 'unknown projectile', none attributed by UKMTO. The human toll may be lower than 11-18 recorded: if Sonowal's Navig8 Messi statement stands, only the Tara Gas seafarer is missing; ADNOC has not reconciled. Still no death or sinking confirmed. Vessel name for 212 and any UKMTO 213 for Iran's claimed mine strikes not surfaced.

items.name: Blockade regime tightens on both sides: CENTCOM advisory (18 Nov) - any ship receiving Iran-origin cargo by ship-to-ship transfer 'may be considered to be evading the blockade' and 'may be stopped, boarded, diverted, captured' with 'use of force consistent with applicable law'; NAVCENT: neutral transit to non-Iranian destinations 'will not be impeded' but subject to visit and search; Iran's navy/IRGC claim five mined tankers in 17 hours and repeat 'Passage through the waterway must be coordinated with Iranian authorities'
items.headline: U.S. Targets Ship-to-Ship Transfers in Expanded Iran Maritime Blockade / Iran Claims 3 Tankers Hit Mines East of Hormuz After Muscat Talks Fail / Five Tankers Claimed, Two Struck
items.claim: gCaptain/Reuters (18 Nov 10:38 PST): CENTCOM advisory issued Wednesday - 'Any ship that receives cargo via a ship-to-ship transfer with a vessel subject to the blockade' (cargo loaded at an Iranian port or coastline) may be 'considered to be evading the blockade' even if it never enters Iranian waters; such ships 'may be stopped, boarded, diverted, captured' or directed to the Iranian port of origin; non-compliance with lawful orders risks enforcement 'including the use of force consistent with applicable law'; NAVCENT: 'The blockade will not impede neutral transit passage through the Strait of Hormuz to or from non-Iranian destinations', neutral vessels 'may still be subject to the right of visit and search'. Blockade timeline: imposed 13 Apr, lifted June, reimposed 14 Jul. Iran side (Treadstone 71/Mehr): regular navy 23:51 Tehran 18 Nov - three 'violating' tankers hit mines east of Hormuz and caught fire; IRGC navy 13:52 Tehran 19 Nov - two 'violating supertankers' with 'more than 4 million barrels' hit mines and exploded; ANI/IRIB IRGC line: 'Passage through the waterway must be coordinated with Iranian authorities'. houseofsaud: Reuters could not confirm; no vessel, flag, owner or insurer named.
items.source: gCaptain/Reuters 18 Nov 10:38 PST; Treadstone 71 19 Nov; houseofsaud 19 Nov 01:25Z; financefeeds 19 Nov (Reuters via CNBC); Iran International summary 18 Nov (CENTCOM 'seizure or military force' paraphrase)
items.note: Both regimes hardened in the same 24 hours: the US closes the Gulf-of-Oman STS loophole (Kpler had 2.60 mb/d of Iran-region flow moving by STS to 11 Nov), and Iran escalates its 'coordination' claim with unverified mine strikes on 'violating' hulls. Neither is a deal tell; both raise the cost of the status quo for Iranian exports and for uncoordinated transits. Muscat 'no deal' context already recorded 11-17. Candidate tell labelled M1 (blockade/transit regime) - scorer maps.

items.name: Houthi missile debris damages the 80-storey PIF headquarters tower in Riyadh (19 Nov; coalition 'addressed a missile threat', 'material damage currently being surveyed'); coalition intercepts cruise missiles toward Riyadh and the south 18-19 Nov, destroys a Dhamar launch platform and 60 targets; Reuters: Saudi preparing for the Yemen war to last into 2027; Yemen designates the Houthis a terrorist organisation; Belgium to seek EU listing; Iran's 18 Nov Kuwait/Bahrain attacks intercepted without damage
items.headline: Middle East war: Riyadh skyscraper damaged, tanker hit near Oman as Trump weighs fresh Iran strikes / Saudi-led Coalition says missile launch platform destroyed in Yemen's Dhamar / Saudis preparing for Yemen campaign to last well into 2027, sources tell Reuters
items.claim: Gulf News (19 Nov 12:13 UAE): a Riyadh tower housing the Public Investment Fund headquarters was damaged - witnesses say the 80-storey tower in the financial district; coalition spokesman al-Malki: the coalition 'addressed a missile threat launched by the terrorist Houthi militia towards Riyadh', 'Initial assessment indicates the impact of debris, with material damage currently being surveyed'. CBS (18 Nov 12:37pm ET): explosion heard in Riyadh as the coalition reports intercepting Houthi cruise missiles and drones; (5:28am ET) coalition says strikes destroyed '60 legitimate military targets', Houthis say at least 17 killed; (11:15am ET) Reuters: Saudi Arabia preparing for its Yemen war to last into 2027, citing Western officials. Iran International (19 Nov 04:14Z): coalition intercepted a Houthi cruise missile toward southern Saudi Arabia and destroyed a launch platform in Dhamar; (07:09Z) Belgian Defence Minister Francken: Belgium will seek EU terrorist listing for the Houthis, 'just another snake of the evil Medusaregime in Tehran'. Khaleej (21:14 UAE 18 Nov): Yemen's government designates the Houthis a terrorist organisation, FM Al-Zouba: 'I call on Yemen's partners to take similar steps'. Gulf front: Iran's 18 Nov drones at Ali Al-Salem (Kuwait) and Bahrain intercepted, no damage or casualties (Gulf News); Kuwait condemns 'dangerous escalation', UAE and Saudi condemn (Khaleej 11:14, 15:51, 17:37 UAE); Saudi civil-defence alerts Najran/Jazan/Khamis Mushait and Sharurah, all cleared.
items.source: Gulf News live 19 Nov 12:13 UAE; CBS live 18 Nov 5:28, 11:15 AM, 12:37 PM ET; Iran International liveblog 19 Nov 04:14Z, 07:09Z; Khaleej Times live 18 Nov; DTN 18 Nov (Saudi 2027 assessment as a price driver)
items.note: First physical damage in Riyadh's financial district in this phase (debris, not a direct hit; PIF tower symbolic). The Houthi front is now the main kinetic driver of Gulf risk while the Iran-Gulf drone exchange of 17-18 Nov was fully intercepted; no further Iranian strike on Kuwait/Bahrain/Saudi dated 18 Nov after 12:11Z or 19 Nov surfaced, and no new US strike on Iran. Houthi East-West pipeline claims of 17 Nov already recorded; no new pipeline claim in gate. EU Houthi listing is a Red Sea/Aspides-adjacent item; no Aspides/Hormuz escort decision found.

items.name: IAEA plumbing: Baghaei rebukes Grossi's 'no double standard' remark - 'This response confuses formal legal status with institutional responsibility and impartiality' (19 Nov); Grossi calls the US-Saudi civil nuclear agreement 'very satisfactory' (18 Nov); Iran's inspection freeze ('no inspections until war ends', 16 Nov) unchanged
items.headline: Gulf News live 19 Nov 08:21 UAE / CBS live 18 Nov 8:39 AM ET
items.claim: Gulf News (19 Nov): Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei criticised IAEA chief Rafael Grossi over his remark that there was no 'double standard', saying 'This response confuses formal legal status with institutional responsibility and impartiality.' CBS (18 Nov 8:39am ET): Grossi called the US-Saudi civil nuclear agreement 'very satisfactory'; Trump has said moving forward is contingent on Saudi Arabia joining the Abraham Accords. Trump at Shenzhen (19 Nov 09:25Z): 'We're not going to let Iran have a nuclear weapon'; the trilateral declaration commits the three to a dialogue on preventing nuclear proliferation without naming Iran.
items.source: Gulf News live 19 Nov 08:21 UAE; CBS live 18 Nov 8:39 AM ET; Iran International liveblog 19 Nov 09:25Z
items.note: Negative IAEA tell: Tehran is contesting the agency's impartiality (the Saudi deal and the 'double standard' line) rather than discussing access; no Grossi-Iran contact, no inspection, no Board item dated in gate. Candidate tell T2 (IAEA/nuclear access) - scorer maps.

items.name: Oil structure: WTI -3.2% to a 12-week low and Brent -1.28% on EIA crude +3.38 mb (vs an expected draw) and gasoline +5.19 mb; Brent-WTI widens $1.80 to 8.93 on tanker freight; Bloomberg - 'very limited appetite to buy the dip', market 'acclimated' to Gulf flare-ups, 'December doldrums'; DTN - Gulf output 'approached pre-war levels', flows 'stabilizing' under US escorts; Vortexa: smaller tankers moved ~2 mb/d out of Hormuz in October; LSEG: flows 'cannot yet normalize'
items.headline: WTI Down 3% as US Crude Build Adds to Global Supply / Oil Falls 3% Despite Middle East Attacks / Morning Highlights: Oil Slips on Large US Stock Build as Attacks Near Hormuz Limit the Decline
items.claim: DTN (18 Nov 2:06pm CST): WTI Dec 83.26 (-2.75, low 81.97), Brent Jan 91.95 (-1.19, low 90.34); EIA week to 13 Nov crude +3.38 mb vs an 18 kb draw forecast, distillate +1.571 mb, gasoline +5.192 mb; WTI -6% over three sessions, Brent -4% this week after -3% and -16%; Brent-WTI spread +$1.80 to 8.93 'tied to elevated tanker freight costs constraining U.S. export arbitrage'; Gulf production 'has approached pre-war levels, with maritime flows stabilizing and U.S. naval security escorts in place'; risk premiums 'compressed ahead of' the Shenzhen talks; IEA (13 Nov) Q4 surplus the main driver; Saudi assessment of a Houthi war into 2027 a risk to Red Sea routes and pipelines. Bloomberg via Rigzone (4:14pm EST): Brent has lost about a fifth this month 'partly because Trump has held off on resuming all-out hostilities'; preliminary vessel data show Hormuz transits 'may be falling month-on-month' but the size is unclear; Babin (CIBC): 'There seems to be very limited appetite to buy the dip'; Molchanov (Raymond James): flare-ups 'a fact of life throughout the past nine months... acclimated to these episodes, just as long as there is no return to all-out war'; Cunliffe (Onyx): 'December doldrums have come early'; Waller: Fed may need more aggressive hikes with inflation partly war-driven. cornerstonefutures (18 Nov 6:45am ET): LSEG - Hormuz flows cannot yet normalise under current conditions; Vortexa via Bloomberg - smaller tankers moved ~2 mb/d out of Hormuz in October, highest since the war began. Thu Asia: Brent 92.12, WTI 83.17; ING sees a more comfortable supply position.
items.source: DTN 18 Nov 2:06pm CST; Bloomberg via Rigzone 18 Nov 4:14pm EST; cornerstonefutures 18 Nov 6:45am ET; cappnotes 18 Nov; Reuters via financefeeds 19 Nov 07:30 GMT
items.note: O-panel headline: four tanker hits, a US-Iran strike exchange and five Iranian mine claims could not stop a 3% WTI break to the lowest close since 26 Aug - the market is pricing surplus, bypass volumes and escorted flows over Hormuz risk, and Brent-WTI widening on freight says the constraint has migrated from the Strait to tanker availability. DTN 'approached pre-war' and Reuters 'roughly pre-war' flow claims again conflict with hormuz.now 7% / tankers 4% / PortWatch 2.3 transits per day and Bloomberg's 'may be falling m/m' - different methods, flagged, not reconciled. Energy equities -3.27% (cappnotes).
